message.reasoning_content:
Job already exited? That was fast. Wait, bench sleeps 120... but job says exited 0. Hmm, maybe it was already... anyway let's check log.

First let's understand the failures. The report failures are cases. Actually wait — the failures may be cases where cycle exists but order.sh doesn't detect it. Let me examine the current order.sh: it prints partial order and exit 0. Also it prints only nodes... hmm, need[] counts only nodes that need something. Nodes that have no outgoing dependency get need=0 and get queued. Nodes that have dependencies get need incremented. Fine.

But there's also a bug: `need[$1]++` — if duplicate edges removed, ok. But the check also requires "every package once, and count matches number of distinct packages". The topological algorithm seems maybe fine. But it also needs the output to include all nodes. Let's just rewrite order.sh with proper Kahn + cycle detection in awk.

Wait, also failures might be due to self-loops? a==b avoided. Duplicates fine.

Let me check: the bug list. The TODO says cycle branch missing. Also potential bug: the queue order iteration over `edge` modifies need while iterating... Actually `for (k in edge)` and decrement — for a given p, each edge k with a[2]==p decrements need[a[1]]. That's once per edge. Fine. But when a node is enqueued then later more edges? No.

Hmm, but there may be another subtle bug: when a node has need[p]==0 at start it is queued even if it also has self-dependency? Not relevant.

Actually key bug: duplicate edges are deduped, good. But the cycle detection missing.

Why do so many cases fail though? Because cycles produced partial order but also because... let's count report failures = 185. Let's test a case manually.

Let me write a proper awk: build adjacency, Kahn with deterministic order, and detect leftover nodes (cycle). Then for the cycle line, need "the packages in it" — suite only checks `$order == cycle:*` and rc==1. So any non-empty list works. But be accurate-ish: print leftover nodes in the cycle.

Note the suite check for cycle: cyc from its DFS. If cyc==1 requires rc==1 and output starts with "cycle:". Otherwise requires rc==0 and valid order with all packages exactly once.

Important: when not cyclic, output must have exactly one line per package, no duplicates, and count == distinct packages. Also all packages appearing in edges. Note package with only incoming edges included via need[$2].

Let me write new order.sh:

awk '
{ e[$1 SUBSEP $2]=1; nodes[$1]=1; nodes[$2]=1 }
END {
  for (k in e) { split(k,a,SUBSEP); adj[a[2]] = adj[a[2]] " " a[1]; indeg[a[1]]++ }
  # count
  n=0
  for (p in nodes) if (indeg[p]+0 == 0) q[++n]=p
  head=1; out=0
  while (head<=n) {
    p=q[head++]; print p; out++
    m=split(adj[p], ch, " ")
    for (i=1;i<=m;i++) { c=ch[i]; if (--indeg[c]==0) q[++n]=c }
  }
  if (out < length(nodes)) { line=""; for (p in nodes) if (indeg[p] > 0) line = line (line==""?"":" ") p; print "cycle: " line; exit 1 }
}' "$file"

Need exit status: awk exit 1 works. But careful: if all fine exit 0.

Deterministic order matters? The suite doesn't require specific order, just validity. Order within queue arbitrary fine.

Also nodes count: `for (p in nodes)` — length(nodes) works in awk.

Edge case: self-loop a==b would give indeg>0 and cycle detected. Fine.

Another subtlety: duplicate edges — deduped by e[]. Good.

Also need to handle the case where the same node appears only as $2: nodes[$2]=1 yes.

Let me also check the sorting determinism isn't needed. Fine.

Let me write the file and run suite. Also check bench log. Also read the rest of the report to be sure of the failure modes and summary line.
